findings.text: The replay checks the critic at each issue branch's head, but at least two of the three "known misses" were never in that diff. The catalog trailer broke catalog-check "on release/v0.58" (fixed by 2032428), and the missing os/exec import was in "its pick to the release branch" (8a847f5). So line 28 compares the critic against faults it could never have seen. That makes the hit rate 0 or a hand-waved "would have", and the tuning in line 68 is driven by misses that don't belong to the input. Either replay the release-branch pick commits themselves, or drop those two from the "known misses" and say why.
Neither criterion can fail on what matters:

Adding `--output-format json` and Unwrap changes how every live critique gate reads its output, yet line 46 says the gate's rules are out of scope. Nothing covers a JSON envelope that is itself an error: `is_error`, `subtype: error_max_turns`, or a usage-limit result like comment 5 at line 109. Unwrap would hand Parse an empty or error `result`. Whether that becomes "failed" or "clear" is unspecified. There is no Must not for "an error result must never record as clear", and no test for it next to TestUnwrapPlainOutput (line 95).

The real-token cap ("5 issues per pass") and "mem-guard check before each run" sit only under Dependencies. Neither is a Must not with a test. Nothing stops tools/critique-replay from running more than 5, re-running a pass, or starting while mem-guard says BLOCKED. Routing may also hand the run to codex while claude is resting, which leaves the cost "—" (line 44) and the before/after token comparison meaningless. The tool should refuse more than 5 issues, refuse when mem-guard blocks, and pin the agent to claude.

The design says "clarify by the issue's updated date", but no `updated` field exists in the issue format. The frontmatter here has only created and started_at. The source of that date isn't stated: file mtime? The date on the answer line? So the clarify range can silently be wrong. The fix is to name the date: for example, the newest `**Answer:**` date, or the D-n date.
"cleared: fixed = a later clear run from the same status" doesn't cover these cases:

The Must not tests only that --out is refused inside an issues dir. It doesn't check that the sandbox clone and its throwaway worktree are outside the live repo's .worktrees, or that the copied issue file can't be the live one. The critic gets "paths only" (line 66), so a path pointing into the live checkout would make it read the live board.

This issue's own first critique run failed on a codex usage limit. The limit text was still parsed into findings ("three blocks", "no Coverage"). That is a live case of the failed-run counting from line 44, and is worth including in the TestStatsSpecFlowSection fixtures.

findings.text: The design doesn't say which version of the issue file the replay gives the critic. Line 66 says only "an issue file copy". Today's copies of the done issues hold hindsight: their status is done, they have later comments, post-mortem links and "fixed by" notes. A critic briefed with them can "catch" the @media or import miss by reading about it. That inflates the hit rate and makes every before/after number in the line 68 tuning wrong. Name the source, for example the issue file as it stood on main at the testing → shipping head (`git show <sha>:issues/...`), with the comments block stripped of anything dated after it. Add a Must not with a test that fails when the copied file mentions a fix SHA (365c0ae, 2032428, 8a847f5) or has a comment dated after the head.

This criterion can't fail. If there are no tuning commits, `git log --grep='^Replay: before' main` prints nothing and still counts as met. "Each tuning commit" has no list to check against. The command also doesn't check that the "after" numbers came from a committed replay pass and weren't typed in. Make it fail: name the expected changes, or a test over tools/critique-replay/testdata. For example, every commit touching internal/critique/brief.go or the criteria lint after 213c968/796483a carries `Replay: before … after …`, and the after numbers match a committed `replay-*.jsonl` pass.

The same 5 issues are used to tune and to score, and the true/false labels are written by hand (line 114, D-3), apparently by the same agent doing the tuning. Nothing stops the brief's Look for list from overfitting to the three named faults ("check @media blocks close", "check imports after a pick") and then reporting 3/3. Add a Must not: the brief names no fault specific to a replayed issue. Also add one or two held-out done issues scored only after tuning, or have someone other than the tuner do the labels.

The "41k tokens" figure has no definition. The design doesn't say whether it includes cache read and write tokens. Those usually dominate and swing between runs, so "tokens before/after" (line 68) may only measure cache luck. Pick one figure (for example input + output, with cache shown apart) and use it in the comment, the stats and the Replay lines.

The proposal to have Parse keep indented continuation lines changes what every live gate reads. Line 46 puts the gate's rules out of scope, yet a continuation line beginning "- blocks …" could become a new held finding, or get swallowed into the one above it. If this route is taken, it needs a Must not with a test: a continuation never turns into its own finding, and a severity line is never absorbed.

D-1 to D-3 are all "YOLO, provisional". The owner's quoted approval (line 14) predates this design and covers the epic's five pieces, not the measuring or the replay's real-token spend. They wait for review after the fact.

The first critique run's earlier blocks are answered in the text: release-branch probes, error envelopes, the cap and mem-guard guards, the clarify date and the cleared rules. No new critique run clearing them is recorded among the comments yet.

findings.raw: blocks issues/Factory/spec-flow-in-use-measure-the-critic-clarify-round-red-rounds-and-post-mortem-on-real-issues-and-tune-them.md:66,105,118 — The hindsight guard only checks the issue copy. The critic itself runs in a worktree of a sandbox clone, and that clone holds main's later history: the fix commits 365c0ae, 2032428 and 8a847f5, their messages ("unclosed @media", the import), and the release/v0.58 branch. A read-only critic that can run `git log`/`git show` (or simply reads a newer file through the clone's refs) can find the fault in that history. That inflates the hit rate, and every before/after number gets worse along with it. TestAsOfCopyHasNoHindsight can't catch this. The fix is to cut the clone at the head (a shallow clone or one with only the head ref, no refs past the head's commit time) and add a Must not with a test that fails when the sandbox can reach a fix SHA.

blocks issues/Factory/spec-flow-in-use-measure-the-critic-clarify-round-red-rounds-and-post-mortem-on-real-issues-and-tune-them.md:68,95,107,29 — The tuning has no signal to tune on. Of the three known misses, two count only at probe (b), so the at-gate hit rate rests on one fault: the @media. The critic is an LLM, so it varies from run to run, and each issue runs once per pass. A before/after of 0/1 → 1/1, or one false block fewer, can't be told apart from rerun noise. TestTuningLedgerMatchesReplayPasses only checks that the ledger's numbers add up; a change that made no difference, or made things worse, passes it. The fix is either to require each issue to run N≥2 times per pass and keep a change only if the gain is bigger than the run-to-run spread on the unchanged brief, or to state that the numbers are anecdotal and ship no brief change on them.

should issues/Factory/spec-flow-in-use-measure-the-critic-clarify-round-red-rounds-and-post-mortem-on-real-issues-and-tune-them.md:97,112 — The cap counts "distinct issues in one --pass", not runs. Retries after a failed run (a usage limit, a timeout) and the two-point probes (a)+(b) per miss are uncapped, and nothing limits how many passes run. So "Must not spend past the cap" doesn't stop what it names. Cap runs per pass (5 gate runs + 3 probes, no automatic retry), say what happens after a failed run, and say what the tool does when mem-guard isn't installed (it's an optional tool per CLAUDE.md): refuse, or run.

findings.text: The clarify date covers only owner answers (newest **Answer:** date) and only-open issues (created). Per the epic's question format (epic line 29), `**Answer:** assumed [n] — <reason>` has no date. An issue with assumed answers only, or assumed plus open, has no rule, so YOLO issues (this one included) land in the wrong range or none.

"Not included: changing the critique gate's rules" doesn't hold literally. Two cases are open: a JSON envelope cut short by a timeout or kill (it falls back to raw stdout, which has no Coverage line, so it holds), and valid JSON with no `result` field. The design should say these hold as failed, and TestUnwrapErrorEnvelopeFails should cover them.

findings.text: The hindsight cut is too coarse and the check is too narrow. D-n decisions are dated by day only ("2026-10-31"), and the replayed issues were done this week, often on the day of their head. "Dropped when dated after the head" therefore keeps every same-day decision made after the head. Body text written later outside the four dropped sections also stays: Approach notes, test notes, "fixed in …". The refusal list has three SHAs plus "unclosed" and "missing import". It misses the other two faults' own words ("@media", "trailer", "Catalog:", "os/exec", "release/v0.58", "pick") and short SHAs of other lengths. The hit rate can still be inflated through text the test doesn't scan. Cut by comment timestamp and by the head commit's own copy where one exists, and refuse on each fault's own words, not only the fix's words.

TestSandboxReachesNoLaterCommit only proves that git in the sandbox can't reach a later commit. Claude's Read, Grep and Glob take absolute paths, though. A critic with read access can open the live checkout or the live issues dir (where the done issue, its retro and the post-mortem name the fix) unless the run is confined to the sandbox. "The critic can't run git" doesn't cover this. Add a Must not with a test that the replay argv limits reads to the sandbox, for example by adding the sandbox dir only and denying paths outside it. The hindsight guarantees at lines 105 and 129 rest on this.

findings.raw: should issues/Factory/spec-flow-in-use-measure-the-critic-clarify-round-red-rounds-and-post-mortem-on-real-issues-and-tune-them.md:68,109,115,29 — The cap allows at most 2 passes ("before, after"). findings.raw: blocks issues/Factory/spec-flow-in-use-measure-the-critic-clarify-round-red-rounds-and-post-mortem-on-real-issues-and-tune-them.md:29,114 — The acceptance criterion and the noise rule ask for opposite things. AC4 (TestTuningLedgerMatchesReplayPasses) fails unless tuning.json has "at least one change". Line 114 says a brief change that doesn't beat the run-to-run spread "is reported and not shipped". At the gate, the tuning set has one catchable fault (the @media); the other two only show at the probe, which doesn't count. With 2 runs per point, no content change can honestly clear the noise floor. So the only way to pass AC4 is to ship the format change, or to ship a change the design's own rule rejects. AC4 should accept a ledger of changes that were measured and not shipped, with their numbers. Otherwise the test pushes toward overfitting, which lines 107 and 114 exist to prevent.

findings.text: This conflicts with the epic's D-4 ("4. Let's make it 4 to start": stop after four red rounds and ask the owner). The design says the critique gate held four times on this issue with no question raised. Instead of raising that now, the issue keeps redesigning and defers it to "the report" at the end of the work. The owner's cap exists so that a fifth fix round goes to the owner first. Before another round, the issue should raise a question: red rounds: (or a ## Clarify question) for the owner. Putting it in a later report sidesteps the rule this issue is meant to measure.

findings.raw: should issues/Factory/spec-flow-in-use-measure-the-critic-clarify-round-red-rounds-and-post-mortem-on-real-issues-and-tune-them.md:115,127,134 — The run cap contradicts itself. Line 115 says "at most 2 passes … 28 runs in all"; line 127 allows pass 3 and "at most 35 runs". The only test that enforces a cap, TestCapAndMemGuard, checks just the distinct issues per pass and mem-guard. Nothing refuses a 4th pass, a 15th run in a pass, or a re-run of an earlier pass, so "Must not spend past the cap" isn't backed by any check. Pick one total, and have the tool refuse past it by counting the runs already in the replay record.

findings.text: The canary can pass without testing anything. "Refuses to start unless the read was denied" doesn't say how a denial is detected (for example permission_denials in the JSON envelope). It also doesn't cover the case where the model never tries the read. A run with no read attempt must count as a canary failure, not a pass. The design also doesn't say whether the Read(//…/**) deny rules cover Grep and Glob, which also take absolute paths. TestArgvDeniesLiveReads only checks the argv text.

The hindsight scan drops any body line containing "@media", "trailer", "picked" or "Catalog: n/a". Those words can be the issue's own spec: a responsive-layout requirement, or a Proves: trailer rule. Cutting them takes requirements out of exactly the area where the fault was, which pushes the hit rate toward a miss. A count per issue shows that lines were lost, not which ones. List the removed lines in the report so the owner can judge each copy.

This line still says "clarify by the issue's updated date". Lines 98 and 116 replaced that with the newest Answer: date, then the newest D-n date, then the created date. The stale line will mislead whoever implements Gather. Fix line 63.

findings.raw: should issues/Factory/spec-flow-in-use-measure-the-critic-clarify-round-red-rounds-and-post-mortem-on-real-issues-and-tune-them.md:26,65 — No acceptance criterion or test covers `issue-cli stats --spec-flow` and its --json, or the "Spec flow: N critique runs…" line in plain stats (line 83). findings.text: Gather is built with the cached aggregate in stats_cache.go. The design doesn't say when that cache is invalidated, so a critique run that just finished may not show in the Spec flow section until the cache refreshes.
